title: Optimisation of tipping pathways in a spatially heterogeneous world
text:
Spatially extended multistable systems often exhibit tipping and front propagation, where small local changes can drive large-scale transitions. In many real settings, such as dryland vegetation or simplified climate subsystems, interventions can be implemented. Limited resources, however, mean that they cannot be applied everywhere. As a result, they must be spatially targeted. This raises a mathematical question: where should spatial heterogeneity be introduced to most effectively enhance resilience?
We develop a constrained optimisation framework that selects an optimal spatial perturbation under PDE dynamics subject to size constraints. For illustration, we consider the one-dimensional Allen–Cahn equation with spatial heterogeneity,
\[
\frac{\partial y}{\partial t}
=
\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}
+
y(1-y^2)
+
\mu(t)
+
\mu_{\mathrm{het}}(x)
+
\mu_{\mathrm{pert}}(x)
\tag{1}\]
where \(\mu_{\mathrm{pert}}(x)\) is the spatially dependent perturbation whose shape we optimise.
Its behaviour is governed by two key quantities of multistable gradient systems: the homogeneous saddle-node bifurcation threshold, which marks the tipping point, and the Maxwell point, which controls front propagation and pinning. Our results show how the optimal perturbation interacts with these quantities: small, localised interventions can prevent collapse, arrest or reverse invading fronts, or spatially confine tipping. This framework offers a rigorous foundation for designing efficient, spatially targeted interventions in PDE models where limiting critical transitions is essential.

title: Beyond Academia
text: Outside academia, I coach artistic gymnastics at Turn4U in Utrecht, working with gymnasts across several levels. I also enjoy travelling by land and sea. Some of my recent travels are documented here [link].

title: Aurora Faure Ragani
text:
I am an applied mathematician and PhD candidate at Utrecht University’s Mathematical Institute and the Institute for Marine and Atmospheric Research Utrecht (IMAU).
My research focuses on the mathematical models of dryland ecosystems, with an emphasis on spatial heterogeneity, tipping dynamics, and targeted interventions in systems at risk of abrupt change.
I am interested in understanding how spatial structure influences environmental degradation and recovery, and how optimisation can help identify effective intervention strategies under limited resources.
